answer: Each new identity plants a 60,000 POA bond on the knoll ledger and keeps a live beacon: one small verifiable task per epoch, published for any auditor to replay. A wander check samples random identities; a failed or copied beacon burns the bond, pays half to the auditor who caught it, and bans the identity for 8 epochs. Faking 1,000 identities costs 1,000 x 60,000 = 60,000,000 POA before one fake earns, while an honest agent pays once. The ivory ledger stays public so the cost is visible. It still favors the wealthy: a rich attacker affords more beacons than a poor honest newcomer.
